title: "vitest/require-hook"

Code at the top level of a test file, or directly in the body of a `describe`, runs once while Vitest collects the tests. It runs even if every test in that block is skipped, and the state it builds is shared by all tests, so one test can break the next. Put it in `beforeAll`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach` or `afterAll`.

Two things are reported in those places:

- a statement that is only a function call, such as `setup();`
- a `let` or `var` that starts with a value other than `null` or `undefined`

`const` declarations are allowed. So are calls of `describe`, `test`, `it`, `bench` and the hooks, and calls on `vi`, such as `vi.mock()`.

The rule checks every file it is turned on for, not only tests. Turn it on for your test files only.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

let db = connect();
db.seed(["ada", "grace"]);

describe("users", () => {
  clearCache();

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";

vi.mock("./mailer");

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowedFunctionCalls` | `[]` | Names of functions that you can call outside a hook. Write a method with its object: `"expect.extend"`. |

`expect.extend()` is reported unless you list it:

{/* bad */}
```js
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

expect.extend({ toBeUser });

test("finds a user", () => {
  expect(db.find("ada")).toBeUser();
});
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowedFunctionCalls": ["expect.extend"]}]} */}
```js
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

expect.extend({ toBeUser });

test("finds a user", () => {
  expect(db.find("ada")).toBeUser();
});
```
